title: Unified time-window index and delta cache for fast paginated rollup queries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Reduce tail latency and read amplification for time-windowed dashboard queries by introducing a unified time-window index alongside a small delta cache for the most-recent writes. Targets: 95th percentile query latency < 150ms for paginated top-K and rollup endpoints (page_size=100) under normal load, and >=5x reduction in backend read IOPS for common dashboards.
rationale: Current dashboard queries scan multiple inverted/time-bucket ranges per tenant, leading to heavy read amplification for high-cardinality filters and frequent pagination jumps. Short-lived recent-event churn (seconds to minutes) further forces repeated index reads. A hybrid approach -- precomputed time-window buckets plus a delta cache for recent events and writes -- reduces the number of shards accessed per query and enables cheap, consistent pagination without re-scanning large index ranges.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile latency for dashboard rollup queries (page_size=100, tenant filter + 7 additional filters) is < 150ms in staging under 1x production QPS
End-to-end reduction of read amplification (datastore read ops) by >=5x on representative dashboard traces
Pagination stability: next/prev cursors remain monotonic and compatible with existing client cursor format; no missing/duplicated rows across pages in acceptance tests
Delta cache invalidation is correct: new events surface in dashboards within 5s by default and can be configured per-dashboard
Safe rollout plan: feature gated, canary on 5% of tenants, metrics and automatic rollback if error rate or tail latency regress by >20%
implementation_notes: Design consists of two parts: (1) a unified time-window index: pre-aggregated, tenant-aware time buckets keyed by (tenant_id, bucket_start, primary_sort_key) stored as small inverted lists that the query planner can union quickly; (2) a memory-backed delta cache for recent writes implemented per-shard with versioned watermarks. Query planner will merge results from the time-window index and the delta cache, then apply top-K/pagination logic on the merged stream. For heavy filters we use bloom-filter assisted sharding to skip buckets. Cursor format will be extended with a stable (bucket_id, offset, watermark) tuple. See design doc for detailed schemas and compatibility notes.
tasks: Design schema for time-window index and bucket size trade-offs (5s, 30s, 1m, 5m)
Prototype delta cache with eviction and watermark propagation
Implement query planner changes to read unified index + delta cache and produce stable cursors
Add bloom-filter metadata to buckets to enable bucket skipping for high-cardinality filters
Run microbenchmarks on staging infra (single-tenant and multi-tenant traces)
Prepare migration scripts and backfill tooling for existing historical buckets
Add feature flags and rollout telemetry (latency, read ops, error rate)
Docs: API changelog for cursor extension and ops runbook for rollback
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Spec drafted. Chosen default bucket size = 30s after analyzing dashboard event time distributions. Linked design doc.
2026-03-11: Delta cache prototype implemented in-memory per-shard; local benchmark shows 3.8x lower datastore reads for recent-window queries (synthetic trace).
2026-03-12: Implemented cursor format proposal and unit tests for monotonic pagination across index+delta merges.
2026-03-13: Integration tests failing on tenant edge case (late-arriving events out-of-order); added watermark-forwarding and re-pagination logic as mitigations.
review_feedback: PM (Rina Gomez): confirm acceptable staleness SLA for dashboards; prefer config per-dashboard with default 5s.
Design (Evan Chen): ensure bucket bloom-filter false-positive rate <=1% to avoid scanning too many buckets; recommended counting-bloom for cardinality-aware accuracy.
Infra (Svetlana Ivanov): watch memory usage of delta cache under bursty writes; suggest LRU+TTL eviction and soft-limits per-tenant.
Security (Omar Haddad): no PII surfaced by caches; ensure KMS-protected audit logs for index mutation operations.
tradeoffs: Storage overhead vs latency: smaller bucket sizes increase index size but reduce read amplification for tight time windows; chose 30s as a pragmatic default.
Complexity of invalidation: versioned watermarks and merge logic are more complex than pure reindexing, but enable lower-latency reads for recent events.
Consistency model: eventual visibility for <5s is acceptable for most dashboards; can enable stronger guarantees for specific customers at cost of read amplification.
benchmarks: Local synthetic trace (10k events/min): baseline 95p latency = 620ms; prototype time-window index + delta cache 95p = 140ms
Read IOPS: baseline ~4200 ops/min for target dashboard; prototype ~700 ops/min (5.9x reduction)
Memory: delta cache steady-state ~120MB per shard under medium load (needs infra gating)
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: unit tests + integration tests in CI -> deploy to staging cluster -> run traffic replay for 24h -> canary 5% tenants for 48h with tight telemetry (latency, error rate, read ops) -> expand 25% -> 100% if stable. Automated rollback if 95p latency regresses >20% or error rate spikes >1%.
monitoring_and_metrics: Per-tenant: median/95/99 latency for dashboard queries
Read ops per query and per-tenant read amplification ratio
Delta cache hit rate and eviction rate
Memory usage of delta cache per-shard
